t:
For payment to the National Service Trust established under subtitle D of title I of the 1990 Act, $208,342,000, to remain available until expended:  Provided, That CNCS may transfer additional funds from the amount provided within “Operating Expenses” allocated to grants under subtitle C of title I of the 1990 Act to the National Service Trust upon determination that such transfer is necessary to support the activities of national service participants and after notice is transmitted to the Committees on Appropriations of the House of Representatives and the Senate:  Provided further, 
That amounts appropriated for or transferred to the National Service Trust may be invested under section 145(b) of the 1990 Act without regard to the requirement to apportion funds under 31 U.S.C. 1513(b).

fable.w: This is an appropriation to the National Service Trust with transfer and investment authority. The tempting reading is that the notice requirement and the phrase "national service participants" signal participation, but the notice goes only to congressional appropriations committees, which are inside the federal government, and "participants" just describes program beneficiaries. No outside party is consulted on or involved in any federal decision.
fable.s: after notice is transmitted to the Committees on Appropriations of the House of Representatives and the Senate

opus.w: This section is an appropriation. Its only procedural step is notice to congressional Appropriations Committees, and Congress is inside the federal government, so that notice is not participation. The word 'participants' in 'national service participants' just names who benefits from the program. No outside party is consulted, no comment period or hearing is required, and no right to sue is granted.
opus.s: after notice is transmitted to the Committees on Appropriations of the House of Representatives and the Senate
opus.b: Two things here look like participation but aren't. First, the phrase "national service participants" uses the word only to describe the people the program serves. Second, the transfer condition requires "notice," but that notice goes to the House and Senate Appropriations Committees, which are part of Congress and so inside the federal government.

qwen_chat.w: The section requires notice to be transmitted to the Committees on Appropriations of the House and Senate before transferring funds. According to the definition, Congress and its committees are inside the federal government. Therefore, this notification is intra-governmental coordination and does not constitute participation with outside parties.
qwen_chat.s: after notice is transmitted to the Committees on Appropriations of the House of Representatives and the Senate
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that notifying the Committees on Appropriations constitutes participation because it involves informing a group before a decision (the transfer of funds) is finalized. However, Congress and its committees are explicitly defined as being INSIDE the federal government. Therefore, notification to them is intra-governmental communication, not participation with outside parties.
